messages:
anna: FYI I'm going to run a short demo tomorrow of conntrack-level telemetry + keystore audit in the onprem lab. want to validate isolation guarantees before we push the shim.

mike: what are the threat vectors you want us to focus on? conntrack leaks? control-plane exposure?

anna: mainly three things: 1) conntrack table visibility from non-privileged namespaces, 2) KMS decrypt request correlation in audit logs (we're missing request_id today), 3) RBAC scope for the keystore-shim svcacct.

lee: for conntrack we can add a netfilter mark and drop conntrack dump from pods that don't have the right mark. plus a NetworkPolicy to deny hostNetwork->pod traffic. quick config snippet: ```iptables -t raw -A PREROUTING -m mark --mark 0x1 -j CT --notrack``` not perfect but reduces accidental exposure.

tara: we should also enforce egress via the keystore proxy only. otherwise decrypt calls can bypass audit. need an admission webhook that injects an egress policy for keystore namespace.

mike: this matches the vuln triage where a mis-scoped svcacct allowed lateral decrypts. we flagged the CVE last month. recommend rotating keys used by that environment and scoping svcacc to minimal verbs.

anna: agreed. Proposed RBAC patch (minimal): ```apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  namespace: keystore
  name: keystore-decrypt-only
rules:
- apiGroups: ["redwood.io"]
  resources: ["keystore/decrypt"]
  verbs: ["create"]```

lee: small nit — prefer resource-level audit annotations so decrypt requests get request_id in logs. we can add an audit hook that injects uuid header.

tara: audit logging item: currently our onprem SIEM ingests /var/log/audit but not the keystore proxy logs. need a short-lived forwarder for demo so we can validate lineage. ops-bot can we spin a forwarder?

ops-bot: infra-check: forwarder image available (registry.redwood/forwarder:canary). permission required: token with project:write.

mike: I'll create the token and limit to the forwarder service account. anna, can you add the request_id header to the shim? we need deterministic tracing for incident playbooks.

anna: yep. will add X-RW-Req-ID header + include keystore request id in audit payload. sample header code: ```reqId := uuid.New().String()
req.Header.Set("X-RW-Req-ID", reqId)``` 

tara: incident response concern — if keystore fails closed we still need to allow healthchecks for autoscaler. propose a fallback route that returns 503 with a structured audit event but doesn't expose plaintext errors.

lee: and add a conntrack threshold alert: host conntrack entries > 500k trigger pager, because high conntrack counts preceded the last blowup.

mike: action items: 1) anna to PR shim changes (req_id + audit payload) 2) lee to draft netfilter+netpol snippet and alert 3) tara to stand up forwarder in lab and run ingest 4) mike rotate environment keys and scope svcacct.

anna: scheduled demo tomorrow 11:00 PT in #eng-security. will show end-to-end: pod -> keystore shim -> forwarder -> SIEM (with correlation). pls bring any test svcacc credentials. :eyes:

mike: noted. I'll bring the scoped token and a quick rollback plan.

tara: thanks — I'll draft the runbook steps for simulated decrypt abuse and an orderly rollback.

lee: one more: consider enabling TLS client certs between shim and keystore HSM endpoint in lab to avoid plaintext auth headers.

anna: good call. will enable mTLS for the demo.

ops-bot: reminder scheduled: deployment window open 11:10-11:40 PT; automated checks will run post-apply.

mike: perfect, see you all then.
